components.name: Two-basin integer quotient/root transport
components.project_addition: Combine the canonical square-collapse basin with exact natural-number floor division to prove that dividing any state of one square basin by an integer d>=2 can move the integer square-root index to only two adjacent values while the base quotient-root index strictly decreases; then use the established quotient composition identity to flatten multi-stage divisor paths to one product divisor, preventing exponential final root-index branching, and prove that for k>=3 the actual quotient root strictly descends below k. The project-specific content is the basin-level compatibility, path-flat two-basin consequence, and strict square-root descent; Nat.nthRoot, floor-division order lemmas, and Nat.div_div_eq_div_mul are established formal tools.
